source_text: Confitebitur peccatum; offeret feminam de grege. Confessio praecedit munus. Christus agnus; anima paenitens ovis.
orientation: Origen is explaining the order of the sin offering: confession of sin comes before the gift, and the female animal from the flock signifies Christ as lamb and the penitent soul as sheep.
pass_a_gloss: He will confess the sin; he will offer a female from the flock. Confession precedes the gift. Christ is the lamb; the penitent soul is the sheep.

choices.why: Keeps the literal gender and source of the animal, which Origen will interpret spiritually as the soul.
Renders the offering as a gift, preserving the sense of something presented to God, distinct from sacrificium.
Keeps the noun-adjective structure and the moral sense of the soul that repents.
Distinguishes the adult sheep from the lamb (agnus), preserving the contrast between Christ and the soul.

bible_refs.note: Confitebitur peccatum; offeret feminam de grege

pass_b_english: He will confess his sin and offer a female from the flock (Leviticus 5:6). Confession comes before the sacrifice. Christ is the lamb; the penitent soul is the sheep.

problems.why: 'Munus' here means sacrifice/offering, not 'gift'; glossary bans 'gift'.
problems.ruling: 'Munus' in Lev 5:6 context means offering/sacrifice; 'gift' misleads and violates stated glossary constraint.

fixed: Changed 'the gift' to 'the sacrifice' because 'munus' here means sacrifice/offering, and the glossary bans 'gift'.
